framework_data.abstract: This paper reevaluates the role of strategic epistemic ignorance in enhancing cognitive reliability, defined as the consistent production of accurate beliefs under normal operating conditions. Contrary to the prevailing assumption that ignorance is inherently detrimental to knowledge acquisition, we argue that deliberately limiting knowledge in specific domains can yield purely epistemic benefits. We identify two primary mechanisms by which strategic ignorance enhances epistemic accuracy: bias prevention and cognitive resource optimization. By preventing the cross-contamination of biases between knowledge domains, strategic ignorance helps maintain objectivity and impartiality. Additionally, optimizing cognitive resources by focusing attention and effort on relevant information enhances understanding and epistemic reliability. Drawing on empirical evidence from cognitive science and examples from scientific practice, we demonstrate how strategic ignorance can be effectively employed to improve the reliability of knowledge production. This conceptual reevaluation challenges the traditional emphasis on knowledge maximization, proposing that selective ignorance can be an integral component of epistemic virtue.
framework_data.main_thesis: Strategic epistemic ignorance, defined as the deliberate limitation of knowledge acquisition in specifically identified domains, can enhance cognitive reliability through bias prevention and cognitive resource optimization, yielding purely epistemic benefits that improve the consistent production of accurate beliefs.
framework_data.core_contribution: By developing a novel theoretical framework that demonstrates how strategic ignorance can lead to purely epistemic benefits, the paper challenges the traditional assumption that knowledge maximization is always epistemically superior and offers new insights into epistemic norms informed by cognitive science.
key_moves: Establish a theoretical framework distinguishing between instrumental and purely epistemic benefits of strategic ignorance, with clear criteria for evaluation
Analyze the dual mechanisms of bias prevention and cognitive resource optimization, demonstrating their interconnected role in enhancing epistemic reliability
Develop empirically-grounded criteria for identifying and evaluating domains where strategic ignorance yields epistemic benefits
Address potential objections, including the knowledge maximization objection, to demonstrate the robustness of the framework
